scope: Complete source-first amount/rate/formula/valuation claim extraction for all 18 previously discovered PHB/DMG monetary groups. This is a research audit only: no catalogs, source census, shared ledger, product bindings, or distribution are changed.
status: private V5 proposal only; not applied; exact V5 source, condition and context review pending

groups.discoveryTitle: Poison cost/dose table and poison manufacture

Assassin training cost is distinct from buying a dose. Materials/bribes per poison is a separate approximate cost.
Experience-point formula/examples on the same page are preserved as excluded XP, not price rows.

groups.tableFocusStatus: six individual row foci include roll, value, category and size.

groups.discoveryTitle: Gem value progression above base value
groups.disposition: Mixed multi-column gem/jewelry valuation section: six d10 adjustment outcomes, 53 stone rows across four base-value classes, seven jewelry bands, plus quantified valuation rules.
dispositionNotes: Full page crop preserves lists split across both columns. Five explicit 5,000-gp gemstone prices are retained; other stones in the “1,000 or more” class are not assigned exact values.
Category headings set shared values for ornamental and semiprecious lists.
Repeated 5,000-gp gem improvement ladder has seven steps; decrease ladder has five denominations.
Jewelry section includes gem-setting exceptional value rule; calculations not printed as a complete exhaustive ladder remain in formula form.
groups.tableFocusStatus: six d10 outcomes and seven jewelry bands are separable; gem lists are multi-column and are highlighted by complete shared-value category spans, not a guessed per-item cell grid.

groups.disposition: Actual scope is a price table, a value-adjustment rule and an 8-line rare-commodity schedule; adjacent armor text is excluded.
dispositionNotes: Footnote applies trimming values to typical garment collars, cuffs and edges.
Right-column armor prose includes “about 2,000 gp” for unusual armor; excluded as adjacent, unrelated armor equipment, not a fur/clothing/rare-commodity line.
groups.tableFocusStatus: fur rows focus the type plus four price columns; adjustment and commodity-rate rows are separately focused.

groups.discoveryTitle: Support, research grants/materials and information discovery
groups.disposition: Multiple sage employment/research schedules: 3 salary/material entries, 7 quantified efficiency/cost rules, 4 information table rows and 2 extra quantified prose cost rules.
dispositionNotes: Information costs may be absent in stated probability circumstances: 20% in relevant general/specific research, and 80% in special category (as described in adjoining note); retain as conditional zero-cost possibility, not a universal free rate.
When the town is not nearby, table time and costs are doubled or travel is separately computed; crop/context indicates this condition.
p33 ship-crew rates in the lower right column are unrelated spillover and excluded; separate hireling/rates material is not merged into this sage scope.
groups.tableFocusStatus: salary and information tables are row-highlighted; prose claims use the complete relevant passage segment, excluding ship-crew passage.

groups.disposition: Actual source has four search-method rows plus separate prose formulas, an worked cost example, and employment-offer terms.
dispositionNotes: Table says inns/taverns cost is “special”; prose supplies drink/barkeep fee, per-10-gp chance and 50-gp ceiling.
The worked example uses 500 gp in tavern/in payments and calculates 63% final effectiveness after overlap.
Initial offer, magic-item interest and quarters/support terms are employment acceptance conditions, not item prices.
groups.tableFocusStatus: four search rows and adjacent prose fee formula are separately highlighted.

groups.discoveryTitle: Town entry, citizenship/class fees, taxes and fines
groups.disposition: Prose-only fee/tax/currency schedule; no formal table is present.
dispositionNotes: Rates, coin denominations, units, frequency and exceptions are preserved; no table rows invented.
Municipal service tithe and organization payments are described without a numeric amount and are excluded from quantified claims; payer-specific conditions remain noted.
Foreign-currency exchange example is a conversion rule, not a general price.
groups.tableFocusStatus: complete contiguous town-charge passage is retained; each distinct rate is assigned a separate focus. Some statements occupy wrapped lines.

groups.disposition: This group is descriptive prose with illustrative treasure amounts/valuations; no table or fixed distribution schedule.
dispositionNotes: Copper/silver/electrum/gold ordering and valuables as possible monster-hoard composition are qualitative and not converted to quantities.
“Gold nobles” is preserved as the source denomination, not silently equated to gp.
The explicit 1,000-gp gem mention is a contrastive non-example: the ogre wealth is not a single gem at that value.
groups.tableFocusStatus: one continuous left-column narrative crop preserves the example chain; individual amounts are parsed as claims, not invented rows.

groups.disposition: Source scope spills over from printed p114 to p115. Contains artifact research price prose, holy/unholy water receptacle price table and formula, then initial spell-research cost/duration prose.
dispositionNotes: p114 artifact type B/C costs are per day/per week, with XP-driven success separate; no cost is inferred from experience points.
Holy-water table distinguishes vessel capacity, basin-cost range, and font cost. Composite price is interpolation formula; defilement is a percentage of the listed normal figures.
p115 continues at top-left; right-column spell-research costs continue onto p116 (source group 11) for success-probability expenditure rules.
Holy-water amounts are manufacturing/receptacle prices, not per-vial prices; only separate vials have a stated unit price.
groups.tableFocusStatus: five metal rows and two adjacent page continuations preserved; table row boxes distinguish metal/capacity/basin/font columns.

sourcePages.role: included direct continuation; row-level sources use this locator

groups.disposition: Contains spell-research success-expenditure threshold prose and potion workshop, upkeep and per-potion cost/time rules; not a price table.
dispositionNotes: Spell success-probability cost schedule lists 2,000/4,000/6,000/8,000 gp additional per spell level with corresponding chance increments; formula preserved as written.
Potion cost is keyed to the XP award in GP; XP remains a separate source field, not currency or treasure.
Alchemist sentence says the time and amount of money are reduced by 50% but phrases the reduction as “of compounding/infusing time”; scope is preserved as a textual uncertainty.
groups.tableFocusStatus: threshold steps and complete potion paragraphs are highlighted; source scan is legible in crop after widening left edge.

groups.disposition: Three-row material cost table; no price ceiling is printed.
dispositionNotes: “And up” is preserved; no maximum price inferred. Failure percentages are conditions, not price modifiers.
groups.tableFocusStatus: three precise rows include material, cost unit and failure adjustment.

groups.disposition: Mixed table: nine monetary-table outcomes, ten combined-hoard result rows, and one map-table result that directs to monetary treasure.
dispositionNotes: d100 bands and dice formulas are transcribed as printed; gem/jewelry piece counts are not assigned gp values here because the passage says value determined later.
The source wording “discounting rolls above 17” is preserved in output text, with the synonym “disregard” flagged as an interpretation, not substituted silently.
Map Table 06-70 is the only map-table outcome that directs to monetary treasure; remaining 3 map outcomes are outside monetary outcome extraction.
Adjacent magic treasure details remain references; XP and encumbrance are not used.

groups.tableFocusStatus: one row focus within complete local Wand of Wonder table context.

groups.disposition: The described page contains no gem-values-by-object schedule; actual priced result is Bucknard’s Everfull Purse coin/gem generation table.
dispositionNotes: Table produces 26 coins of listed denomination(s), not a gem valuation by object. Gem footnote says 10-gp base, up to 100 gp.
The prose preceding the table explains the purse’s once-determined daily replication behavior.
groups.tableFocusStatus: three roll rows include columns CP/SP/EP/GP/PP/Gems; footnote is separate precise focus.

groups.disposition: No gem-price table on this page; only the Deck of Many Things “Gem” card specifies gold jewelry and 1,000-gp base-value gems.

Experience points equal to value and max one level rise are adjacent XP rules, preserved as excluded XP context.
groups.tableFocusStatus: complete Gem-card paragraph is highlighted; no invented total valuation.

groups.disposition: Actual group is a 13-outcome table of Robe of Useful Items patches, with three monetary/valuation results; not a general random-treasure price table.
dispositionNotes: Values are: bag of 100 gp; silver coffer valued at 500 gp; 10 gems of 100-gp value each (1,000 gp combined base).
The rest of the table results are non-monetary items; the table’s roll-twice row is not itself a price.
XP/encumbrance values are not merged; no other value claim in the displayed passage.
groups.tableFocusStatus: all 13 result rows remain together in the context crop; the three monetary rows have individual precise row foci.

groups.disposition: Eight-row d% treasure-generation table; five currency amounts, gem/jewelry quantities and magic result plus a with-monster modifier.
dispositionNotes: Amounts are per level; gems and jewelry are quantities, not priced here.
The with-monster rule calls for two base-table rolls, adding 10% to each roll total.
Adjacent room-trap tables are unrelated and excluded.

exclusions.treatment: Preserved as distinct XP units; not counted as currency/price. Relevant p20 assassin XP example and p143 Gem-card XP award remain adjacent but excluded from amount totals.
No weight or encumbrance values included as money, even when tables use gp abbreviations elsewhere.
Source rows are counted in table denominators, but non-price outcomes (weapons, spells, traps, etc.) are not forced into price records.
Retain ranges, lower-bounds, or unspecified status; do not infer gem base values from material description or other page tables.
Excluded and noted under spillovers, including DMG p25 alignment/upkeep, p27 armor example, p33 ship crew costs, and non-price table sections.

Existing PHB equipment, DMG hireling, service/construction, magic-price and post-p125 selected-item surveys remain separate, potentially overlapping scoped inventories; no deduplication or completeness claim is made here.

uncertainties.item: Poison marks *** and **** are visible in the source table but no corresponding explanations appear in the page footnotes; meanings unresolved.
Entry fee grammar distinguishes citizens/noncitizens and persons/animals/wheels; source wording retained as a conditional phrase rather than normalized to an unambiguous tariff for every case.
Source table says “discounting rolls above 17”; intent may be discard/disregard, but transcription retains printed wording and flags interpretation.
“Gem stones 1,000 or more gp” provides only a lower bound for most listed stones; no precise value inferred. Gemstone/jewelry descriptions and some parenthetical values are incomplete by design.
Alchemist cost/time reduction phrase syntactically unclear; report captures stated 50% cost and time reductions and preserves ambiguity.
The prose example uses “gold nobles” and an unclear 1,000-gp gem contrast; denominations and negative-example status are preserved literally.

spilloverPassages.passage: Assassin XP formula and worked example, plus poison study time; XP and duration are separate, not price rows.
Character expenses, maintenance and atonement values near the gem table are unrelated and excluded.
Opposite armor column includes an approximately 2,000-gp armor note; excluded as outside fur/clothing/rare-commodity source scope.
Lower/right column ship-crew monthly costs are separate hireling content, excluded here; source values not transcribed into this group.
Continuation after printed p114: holy/unholy water table and spell-research initial cost/duration paragraph; included as direct continuation.
Spell-research success-cost rules and potion manufacture text; it is continuation of p115 spell research and also covers potion-workshop costs.
Actual content is Bucknard’s Everfull Purse, not a gem-value-by-object table.
Actual quantified content is Deck of Many Things Gem card; no high-value gem table.
Actual quantified content is one Wand of Wonder row; no gem/magic treasure value table.
Actual quantified rows are three outcomes within Robe of Useful Items table; other nine outcomes are nonmonetary.

verificationNotes: Original source files were SHA-256 verified against the captured census before source review.
PHB 29 fee values were pixel-transcribed from the full row/column table, including printed dashes and the scope footnote.
Actual pixels were inspected for each primary page and relevant continuations; limited crop images and source-page renders remain only in /workspace/scratch/batch5-phb-dmg-prices/.
Source groups misnamed as valuation tables were reclassified from page content and their actual monetary claims enumerated; absent tables were not invented.
No shared ledger, source census, catalog, field binding, tool, handoff, or distribution data was modified by this price extraction task.
All included passages use short structured paraphrases/factual values; no private PDF or full-page scan is included in the repository reports.
